site.name: World Zombie Day: London
site.description: World Zombie Day: London is a free, family-friendly charity zombie walk through central London. Saturday 10 October 2026.
home.hero.title: World Zombie Day: London
home.hero.standfirst: The zombies couldn’t stay buried forever. After a hiatus since 2019, the London branch has been resurrected — and we’re shambling back with more excitement than ever before.
home.essentials.title: The essentials
home.essentials.when.label: When
home.essentials.when.value: Saturday 10 October 2026. World Zombie Day always falls on the second Saturday of October.
home.essentials.where.label: Where
home.essentials.where.value: Central London. The meeting point is confidential and goes out to everyone who registers a few days before the event.
home.essentials.cost.label: Cost
home.essentials.cost.value: Free. There’s an optional “pay what you can” donation — £5 is the suggested amount, and everything beyond running costs goes to the charity.
home.essentials.who.label: Who it’s for
home.essentials.who.value: Everyone. Family-friendly, dog-friendly, and planned with step-free routes for prams and wheelchairs. Under-18s need a parent or guardian with them.
home.essentials.wear.label: What to wear
home.essentials.wear.value: Your best zombie attire is highly recommended but not required. No weapons of any kind, real or fake.
home.about.title: What is World Zombie Day?
home.about.body1: World Zombie Day was born in Pittsburgh’s Monroeville Mall in 2006 — the location of George Romero’s Dawn of the Dead. More than 50 cities worldwide now take part, including New York, Pittsburgh, Paris, Hong Kong, Los Angeles, Chicago, Dallas, Seattle and Tokyo.
home.about.body2: The idea is simple: fans of zombie culture come together, take over a bit of the city for an afternoon, and raise money for a good cause while doing it. London has been shambling since 2011.
home.day.title: What happens on the day
home.day.body1: Hundreds of zombies meet at a confidential starting point in central London, check in with a steward, and shamble a route between locations across the afternoon — groaning, posing for photographs, and collecting donations along the way.
home.day.body2: Stewards in high-vis lead the walk and keep everyone safe at crossings. There are scheduled pauses for photos, so there’s no need to hold up the horde for a shot.
home.charity.title: Who we’re raising money for
home.charity.body1: This year the horde is fundraising for The Dead Good Club, a not-for-profit that helps people reclaim their attention in the AI era and celebrates the community and creativity of horror culture.
home.charity.body2: Brain rot and doom scrolling aren’t a personal failing — they’re the result of systems built to profit from our attention, and the people hit hardest are often the ones whose brains were already wired differently.
home.charity.body3: The club runs programmes on attention, critical thinking, media literacy and ethical technology. The approach is not anti-AI; it is pro-human.
home.cta.title: Join the horde
home.cta.body: Registration is essential — it’s how we send you the meeting point, the route and everything else you need to know.
register.title: Register
register.standfirst: Join the horde. Experience London’s reanimated zombie walk through the heart of the city — don your most impressive zombie attire and shamble with hundreds of others through iconic London locations.
register.status.title: Registration for 2026
register.status.body: Registration is not open yet. This page will carry the link as soon as it goes live — and the meeting point goes out to everyone who has registered a few days before the event.
register.why.title: Why you have to register
register.why.body: Registration is essential to receive the confidential meeting point information, the route, and any safety updates for the day.
register.cost.title: What it costs
register.cost.body: The event is free to attend. There’s an optional “pay what you can” donation — we suggest £5 — and all proceeds beyond operational costs go directly to our charity partner.
register.access.title: Accessible, family-friendly and dog-friendly
register.access.body: Bring the whole horde out for the day. Children with spooky dispositions will enjoy this perfect primer to Halloween. All participants under 18 must be accompanied by a parent or guardian. Well-behaved dogs on leads are welcome to join their undead owners. Accessible routes are planned for prams and wheelchairs.
register.charity.title: Supporting a worthy cause
register.charity.body: This year your support helps The Dead Good Club. Through programmes and resources focused on attention, critical thinking and ethical technology, they help people reclaim their attention and navigate the evolving tech landscape in the AI era.
register.involved.title: Get involved
register.involved.body: Help out by volunteering your time, assisting with fundraising, or simply spreading the word. Get in touch to join the event team.
rules.title: Zombie rules of conduct
rules.standfirst: Put on a good show. Stay in character but don’t get carried away — you are responsible for your own safety and good conduct.
rules.1: Use the “haunted house” rule: you are not to touch anyone.
rules.2: Use your best judgement when planning your outfit. Do not bring weapons — fake, fantasy, or definitely not real. You’ll be on your feet and outdoors for most of the day, so take that into consideration. And be creative!
rules.3: Do not attempt to scare anyone who is not a willing participant. If anyone is freaking out, turn and shamble in the opposite direction. Avoid confrontations.
rules.4: Where the walk is near streets or roadways, stay on the pavement unless crossing. When crossing, it’s fine to break character and cross quickly — think fast “New Dawn of the Dead” zombies rather than the slower “Old Dawn of the Dead” ones. Blocking traffic is a crime and anyone doing so could be arrested.
rules.5: Strictly no illegal drugs, and no alcohol for under-18s. Police will be called if this rule is broken.
rules.6: No littering, destruction of property, or any other illegal activity. That includes smearing fake blood and banging on windows.
rules.7: You might be asked for photo ID at the pubs, and your zombie face might not match it. If you are refused entry, please understand the doorman is only doing his job.
rules.8: Do not attempt to push your way into any business if you are not welcome.
rules.stewards.title: Stewards are there to help
rules.stewards.body: Stewards in high-vis lead the walk, manage crossings and answer questions. If you see any behaviour that concerns you, speak to a steward.
faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.standfirst: Some commonly asked questions and their answers.
faq.a1: Saturday 10 October 2026. World Zombie Day always occurs on the second Saturday of October.
faq.q2: Where will the event take place? How do I get there?
faq.a2: The event details are revealed a few days before the event to everyone who has registered. The locations are typically in central London and easy to reach on the Underground. If you need special arrangements, email megan@worldzombieday.co.uk.
faq.a3: Yes! Bring the whole horde out for the day. Children with spooky dispositions will enjoy this perfect primer to Halloween events. All participants under 18 must be accompanied by a parent or guardian.
faq.a4: Yes, this is a dog-friendly event. Well-behaved dogs on leads are welcome to join their undead owners.
faq.q5: Will there be stairs or accessibility restrictions?
faq.a5: Every effort is made to choose locations that are accessible, but as we head to several locations on the day there may be obstructions or road blocks that require alternative routes.
faq.q6: Is there a specific dress code?
faq.a6: Your best zombie attire is highly recommended, but not required. Please be mindful that this is a public event — you will be seen by locals and tourists of all ages, and are likely to be photographed or filmed.
faq.a7: No. Please do not bring protest signs or use this event for any political agenda or demonstration.
faq.a8: Nothing. The event is free, with an optional “pay what you can” donation — £5 suggested. Everything beyond running costs goes to the charity.
faq.more.title: Still stuck?
faq.more.body: Email megan@worldzombieday.co.uk and we’ll get back to you.
sponsors.title: Become a sponsor
sponsors.standfirst: We are always open to new sponsors — with the primary aim of raising funds for the charity.
sponsors.intro1: Our sponsors help us by contributing directly to our charity of choice, or by helping with our admin costs.
sponsors.intro2: Each year hundreds of enthusiastic zombies take part, and we are typically featured in major publications including Time Out, BuzzFeed, The Guardian and The Huffington Post.
sponsors.options.title: Sponsorship options
sponsors.onsite.title: On-site promotion
sponsors.onsite.body1: As we move from location to location throughout the day, on-site promotion should either be mobile or limited to one stop.
sponsors.onsite.body2: Be creative. We ask that you run any concepts by us so we can make sure they’re aligned with the event and the charity — beyond that you have free rein.
sponsors.onsite.examples.title: Things sponsors have done before
sponsors.onsite.example2: “Breaking news: zombie outbreak reported in central London”
sponsors.onsite.example3: Phone apps reviewed by real zombies
sponsors.onsite.noflyering.title: No flyering
sponsors.onsite.noflyering.body: It’s important to us that nobody hands out flyers or anything else likely to become litter. Stickers or stamps are good alternatives.
sponsors.prize.title: Online prize giveaway
sponsors.prize.body: We typically get 1,500 people registering for World Zombie Day: London. A description of your prize and information about your organisation is shown to everyone who registers.
sponsors.prize.item1: Send us a summary of the prize, its value, and an image or video to advertise it.
sponsors.prize.item2: Include a redemption or promo code, or tell us how the winner will receive the prize. If you have specific terms you use for raffles let us know, otherwise we’ll use a generic set.
sponsors.contact.title: Get in touch
sponsors.contact.body: If you are interested in becoming a sponsor, email megan@worldzombieday.co.uk.
photo.title: Photo policy
photo.standfirst: We love seeing all the wonderful images of you bloody creative zombies after the big day.
photo.intro1: We are ever grateful to everyone who has documented and shared their highlights from World Zombie Day: London. Keep them coming this year.
photo.intro2: All are welcome to photograph or film on the day. Here are some things you should know about our photo and video policy.
photo.basics.1: Filming and photography happen throughout the day — by freelance and vocational photographers, by press, and by our sponsors.
photo.basics.2: If you are attending only to photograph or film, you still need to register to receive the starting location, route and other relevant information.
photo.basics.3: You are not obliged to attend as a zombie, but it is encouraged.
photo.credit.title: Please include this text when you post
photo.credit.body: The purpose of World Zombie Day is to raise money for good causes. Join the zombies in fundraising for The Dead Good Club, committed to fighting brain rot. A not-for-profit pro-human organisation helping people build healthier digital habits in a post-human era. To donate go to: paa.ge/worldzombieday
photo.credit.tags: And please tag anything you post with #WZD2026 and #WorldZombieDay.
photo.rules.title: Rules of engagement
photo.rule1.title: 1. Safety and consent
photo.rule1.item1: Respect a zombie’s wishes if they do not want to be photographed or filmed.
photo.rule1.item2: Do not intentionally obstruct anyone’s path, shop entrances, streets or traffic.
photo.rule1.important: Important: do not hold up the walk for photo shoots or take participants aside. We have agreed timings with the city and disruption has knock-on effects. There are times set aside in the day where we pause for photos — please help us stick to the schedule.
photo.rule2.title: 2. No unauthorised commercial sales
photo.rule2.item1: Photographers may not sell photos directly to event participants.
photo.rule2.item2: Distributing “spec”, proof or access cards for personal financial gain is strictly prohibited.
photo.rule2.item3: Soliciting money, tips or digital payments from guests for photos is banned.
photo.rule3.title: 3. Focus on the cause
photo.rule3.item1: All photographs taken at this event must support the charity’s mission.
photo.rule3.item2: Images should be used to promote the cause, thank donors, or share the event’s success.
photo.consent.title: Consent
photo.consent.body: All those who participate in this event may be filmed and/or photographed, and give consent for any filmed footage or other likeness, picture, photograph, portrait or moving image (in whole or in part) to be used and/or published or broadcast for marketing, social media and public relations purposes without further limitation and in perpetuity.
photo.press.title: Press
photo.press.body: Members of the press: please contact megan@worldzombieday.co.uk with any enquiries, or head to the press kit for logos, photography and boilerplate.
photo.credits.title: The photographers
photo.credits.body: Every photograph on this site was taken by someone who gave their time to the event. Please credit them if you share their work.
press.title: Press kit
press.standfirst: Everything you need to cover World Zombie Day: London — boilerplate, key facts, logos and photography.
press.contact.title: Press contact
press.boiler.short.title: Short boilerplate
press.boiler.short.body: World Zombie Day: London is a free charity zombie walk through central London, held on the second Saturday of October. In 2026 it returns on Saturday 10 October, raising money for The Dead Good Club.
press.boiler.long.title: Long boilerplate
press.boiler.long.body: World Zombie Day is an international annual event that grew from Pittsburgh’s first zombie walk at Monroeville Mall in 2006, the site where George Romero filmed Dawn of the Dead. Its aim is to bring fans of zombie culture together in an international effort to raise money for charity, and more than 50 cities now take part. The London walk has been running since 2011 and typically draws around 1,500 registrations; it returns on Saturday 10 October 2026 after a hiatus, raising money for the not-for-profit The Dead Good Club. The event is free, family-friendly and dog-friendly, and open to anyone who wants to shamble.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.standfirst: How World Zombie Day: London handles your information.
privacy.placeholder.title: This policy is being rewritten
privacy.placeholder.body: The previous privacy policy did not survive the move from our old website. A full policy will be published here before registration opens for 2026.
privacy.interim.title: In the meantime
privacy.interim.body: We collect an email address when you register, and use it only to send you information about the event — the meeting point, the route, and safety updates. We do not sell or share it. To ask what we hold or to have it deleted, email megan@worldzombieday.co.uk.
privacy.photos.title: Photography
privacy.photos.body: This is a public event and participants may be photographed or filmed. See the photo policy for details of what that means and how images are used.
